Subject: DPA & Order Form — transfer assessment and initial questions

Hi Rishi and Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BlueWave is excited about Redwood’s runtime performance. Legal has a few outstanding items before we can circulate the Order Form for signature: primarily the DPA scope and cross-border transfer language. I’ve attached a short questionnaire (BlueWave_DPA_Questions_0505.xlsx) with our primary concerns. Top items:

- Controller/processor mapping: we need explicit language that Redwood is a processor for customer content and will process only per documented instructions.
- SCCs & transfer legal basis: confirm which SCCs you will rely on and provide any transfer impact assessment or UK addendum.
- Subprocessor disclosure and notification timing.
- Audit/evidence: we typically require a rights-to-audit clause; we accept SOC 2 reports but need a right to reasonable on-site audits in exceptional cases.
- Data retention and deletion: confirmation of deletion timeframe after contract termination.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a completed TIA (transfer impact assessment) for EU→US hosting, and whether you can accept our proposed minimal language edits on the Order Form? We’re targeting a PO and signature by end of May if possible.

Thanks — I’ve looped in Ethan (procurement) for order form logistics.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Sr. Legal Counsel | BlueWave Health

Hi Alyssa / Ethan —

Attached are our consolidated redlines and a short cover memo: BWH_DPA_Redlines_20270520.docx and OrderForm_BlueWave_Redlines_20270520.pdf. Summary of our positions and requests below (please consider this Redwood’s starting position — happy to iterate):

Key negotiation points
- Controller / Processor: Redwood confirms we are the processor of Customer Data and will act only on documented customer instructions. We propose a clarification clause referencing the Order Form as the instruction set. (non-negotiable: we cannot accept controller status).

- Standard Contractual Clauses & Transfers: Redwood is prepared to execute the EU SCCs (2021) as revised by the European Commission and to add the UK Addendum where required. For EU→US transfers we will provide a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) summarizing legal landscape, supplementary measures (encryption, access controls, contractorial safeguards), and reliance on SCCs. The TIA will be delivered as a redacted operational summary (no privileged internal assessments) within 5 business days after execution of an NDA or mutual obligations to treat the TIA as confidential.

- Subprocessors: We will provide a current subprocessors list at signature and 30 days prior notice for material changes. We cannot agree to a blanket veto; customers can object to a new subprocessor within 15 days and request mitigation (e.g., SOC 2 evidence or alternative controls).

- Audit Rights & Evidence: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report and, where necessary, supply internal security questionnaires and scoped answers. We cannot routinely accept unfettered on-site audits; for critical healthcare customers we can negotiate a targeted on-site with reasonable notice and limited scope, or provide a third-party assessment instead.

- Data Retention & Deletion: Proposed clause: Redwood will delete or return Customer Data within 60 days after termination of the Order Form unless otherwise required by law. For backups, deletion will occur within 90 days.

Requests for BlueWave
1) Confirm if BlueWave can accept SOC 2 + scoped questionnaire in lieu of general on-site audit for ordinary requests. If not, please provide the specific scope you would require for an on-site review.
2) Confirm whether BlueWave needs the unredacted TIA (our preference is to provide a redacted operational TIA and SOC2 evidence).
3) Any material deviations in your Order Form that would change data flows (e.g., transfer hubs in other regions) — call these out so we can confirm subprocessor mapping.

We’ve attached tracked redlines and a clean marked-up Order Form. If these positions are acceptable, we can produce a DocuSign-ready Order Form and a short MSA amendment with SCCs as an exhibit. Target timeline: final signature by 31 May assuming no major legal issues.

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear positions. A few quick notes from our side:

- SOC 2 + redacted TIA is acceptable in principle; procurement will want to see the TIA redacted summary before final PO.
- We can accept the 60/90 day deletion window with a short carve-out for legal hold subject to prior notice.
- On-site audits: we’ll accept SOC 2 + third-party assessments for now, but reserve the right to request an on-site for critical incidents; we’ll share the proposed scope if that becomes necessary.

Next steps: please send a DocuSign-ready Order Form (with redlines accepted) and the redacted TIA summary to alyssa.chen@bluewavehealth.com and ethan.moore@bluewavehealth.com. If possible, include a short line-item summary of accepted vs. open clauses so procurement can approve the PO. We’re still aiming to sign by 31 May.

Once we receive the DocuSign link we’ll circulate internally and aim to get it to procurement for PO issuance.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Alyssa
